title: Lower CLIF atomics through portal-pc-waffle
description: Lower representable CLIF atomic operations with portal-pc-waffle shared-memory Wasm operators. Keep atomic lowering outside the differential fixture suite because the chosen reference interpreter and Wasmi execution runtime cannot run the needed linear shared-memory atomics.
acceptance_criteria: Default translation rejects atomic CLIF unless shared memory is explicitly enabled; representable operations lower to Wasm atomics and unsupported operations fail clearly; atomic fixtures are intentionally absent with the limitation documented.
notes: Per user direction, removed the atomic smoke fixtures and runner special case. Atomics remain implemented but untested in the committed fixture suite.
close_reason: Atomic lowering is implemented; user-approved scope defers fixture coverage and documents why.

title: Prevent atomics from silently becoming ordinary memory operations
description:
## Context
Atomic load/store, read-modify-write, and compare-and-swap currently lower to ordinary wasm loads and stores. This is only correct under an explicit single-threaded execution contract. Until shared-memory atomics are implemented, reject atomic CLIF operations unless a documented single-thread mode is explicitly selected.

## Steps to Reproduce
Translate a CLIF function containing an atomic load, atomic store, atomic RMW, or atomic CAS and inspect or execute the emitted wasm. The current lowering emits non-atomic memory operations without requiring a single-thread setting.

## Acceptance Criteria
Default translation rejects every atomic opcode with a clear diagnostic. If a single-thread mode is supported, tests demonstrate it is opt-in and document that threaded wasm is unsupported. No atomic operation silently emits non-atomic wasm under the default configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Default translation rejects every atomic opcode with a clear diagnostic. If a single-thread mode is supported, tests demonstrate it is opt-in and document that threaded wasm is unsupported. No atomic operation silently emits non-atomic wasm under the default configuration.
close_reason: Reject atomic load/store/RMW/CAS and fence rather than lowering to non-atomic operations. Add error fixtures checked by the shared runner; cargo test passes.

title: Preserve i8 and i16 semantics across wasm lowering
description:
## Context
The translator maps CLIF i8/i16 values to wasm i32. Current lowering masks only narrow add/sub/mul results, while other operations can consume or produce values whose high bits affect later CLIF operations. Make narrow operand normalization and result truncation consistent across every supported opcode, including signed operations.

## Steps to Reproduce
Translate a function that takes an i8 or i16 parameter and uses it in a bitwise operation, shift, division, or comparison before returning or widening the result. Compare its execution with the Cranelift interpreter, especially for -1 and the type's signed minimum/maximum.

## Acceptance Criteria
Add differential fixtures covering narrow function arguments, bitwise operations, shifts, arithmetic, signed and unsigned comparisons, and narrowing conversions. Results and downstream uses must match the Cranelift interpreter for boundary values such as -1, minimum, and maximum.
acceptance_criteria: Add differential fixtures covering narrow function arguments, bitwise operations, shifts, arithmetic, signed and unsigned comparisons, and narrowing conversions. Results and downstream uses must match the Cranelift interpreter for boundary values such as -1, minimum, and maximum.
close_reason: Normalize i8/i16 arguments and operation operands/results; add differential fixtures for narrow arithmetic, bitwise, shifts, comparisons, extensions, counts, division, and truncation. cargo test passes.

title: Handle CLIF immediate-form scalar opcodes
description:
Why: An alternate generated Cranelift 0.136 opcode inventory includes immediate-form arithmetic, comparison, shift, rotate, division/remainder, and bitwise opcodes not named in the current translator.

Scope: iadd_imm, imul_imm, irsub_imm, icmp_imm, signed/unsigned div/rem immediate forms, immediate shifts/rotates, band/bor/bxor immediate and complement forms.

Acceptance: Confirm which forms are exposed by the configured Cranelift Opcode::all(); lower all exposed supported forms with correct signedness and overflow behavior, and cover them in opcode inventory/tests.

title: Support explicit stack load/store opcodes
description:
Why: An alternate generated Cranelift 0.136 opcode inventory includes stack_load, stack_store, dynamic_stack_load, and dynamic_stack_store forms not covered by the current stack_addr path.

Acceptance: Confirm these forms are exposed by the configured Cranelift Opcode::all(); lower supported accesses with correct frame/dynamic-stack semantics or document why they are outside the backend contract; tests cover supported forms.

title: Lower scalar fused multiply-add
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines scalar fma, which is not covered by current float lowering.

Acceptance: f32/f64 fma preserve single-rounding behavior; tests distinguish fused from separate multiply/add.

title: Handle sequence points
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines sequence_point, whose treatment by this Wasm backend needs to be explicit.

Acceptance: The opcode has a documented handling policy and a coverage test or rationale for safe erasure.

title: Lower integer overflow and carry operations
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines overflow and carry operations that are not covered by existing lowering tasks.

Scope: sadd_overflow_cin, uadd_overflow_cin, signed/unsigned add, subtract, and multiply overflow operations, trapping overflow variants, and overflow-with-borrow forms.

Acceptance: Each supported opcode/type combination returns the correct value and overflow result or traps as specified; tests cover signed and unsigned boundaries.

title: Lower cls and bmask integer operations
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines cls and bmask, which have no lowering in the current translator.

Acceptance: Supported widths match Cranelift semantics, with tests for zero, sign patterns, and boundary values; unsupported widths have explicit diagnostics.

title: Lower conditional traps
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines trapz and trapnz, but current control-flow lowering handles unconditional trap only.

Acceptance: Both opcodes translate correctly for supported integer widths; tests cover true/false conditions and trap codes.

title: Lower remaining select and target-specific operations
description:
Why: Handle select_spectre_guard, bitselect, blendv, and x86 pshufb/pmulhrsw where supported by the selected legalization strategy.

Acceptance: Applicable operations preserve semantics; machine-specific operations are legalized independent of host ISA or explicitly rejected with tests.

title: Add opcode and type coverage audit for Cranelift upgrades
description: Why: Source inspection shows Cranelift exposes Opcode::all() for the version pinned by this crate. Generated build artifacts also differed in opcode count, so the inventory must reflect the actual dependency configuration rather than a hand-copied list.\n\nAcceptance: Add a coverage registry with an explicit status for every Opcode::all() member in the configured build (lowered, intentionally erased, or unsupported with rationale). Ensure a Cranelift upgrade or configuration change that adds an opcode forces inventory review. Track partial type/feature support and document the refresh workflow.

title: Complete tail-call lowering
description:
Why: Tail-call lowering has gaps across supported call forms, signatures, and modes.

Scope: return_call and return_call_indirect, imports, libcalls, object mode, Wasm feature constraints, and shadow-stack cleanup.

Acceptance: Supported tail calls lower correctly; unsupported feature/ABI cases report specific errors; tests cover direct and indirect calls.

title: Lower traps, debug traps, and machine state intrinsics
description:
Why: Machine-specific and trap operations require explicit Wasm/runtime semantics.

Scope: debugtrap, trap, trapz, trapnz, pinned-register operations, frame/stack/return-address access, exception-handler-address operations, and related intrinsics where meaningful for Wasm. Conditional trap work is also tracked in clif2wasm-aaw.15.

Acceptance: Each opcode has a correct Wasm/runtime lowering or an explicit documented unsupported boundary with tests.

title: Support try_call and exception control flow
description:
Why: The bridge does not handle try_call/try_call_indirect exception edges and exception tables.

Acceptance: Supported exceptional control flow translates with correct block arguments and results and has tests; unsupported models are explicitly diagnosed and documented.

title: Lower dynamic stack addresses and stack switching
description:
Why: dynamic_stack_addr and stack_switch are not currently lowered.

Acceptance: Stack operations have a documented ABI/runtime design and correct tests, or precise unsupported diagnostics and rationale.

title: Support TLS and remaining global value forms
description:
Why: Global lowering currently handles limited symbol forms and excludes TLS/dynamic forms.

Scope: tls_value and applicable GlobalValueData forms beyond direct symbols, including dynamic or VMContext forms.

Acceptance: Every intended form resolves correctly or has an explicit documented boundary; tests cover symbol offsets, TLS policy, and object mode.

title: Complete floating-point and narrow conversion coverage
description:
Why: Several float conversion forms and f16/f128 types are not currently supported.

Scope: Missing constants and conversions where Waffle/Wasm can represent or legalize them, plus narrow and i128 float-to-int cases and i128-to-float conversions where possible.

Acceptance: Lowerings preserve NaN, overflow, saturation, and trap behavior, or document the unsupported boundary; tests cover edge cases.

title: Support remaining scalar memory operations and flags
description:
Why: Current memory lowering covers common scalar accesses but not all CLIF access forms or flag combinations.

Scope: Remaining widening/truncating and vector loads/stores where supported, plus memory flags, alignment, offsets, and endianness.

Acceptance: Supported combinations lower correctly; unsupported flags and offsets fail explicitly; tests cover widths and boundaries.

title: Lower SIMD arithmetic, comparisons, and reductions
description:
Why: Cranelift's vector opcode families are absent from the current scalar lowering.

Scope: vector arithmetic and bitwise ops, comparisons, select/blendv/bitselect, reductions (vany_true, vall_true, vhigh_bits), pairwise add, multiply/add variants, and vector float conversion operations where supported.

Acceptance: Supported SIMD families preserve lane semantics; tests cover each selected opcode family and lane type. Unsupported cases are explicit.

title: Complete scalar integer min/max, saturation, and multiply operations
description:
Why: Scalar integer min/max, saturation, rounded average, and high multiply opcodes are missing from current lowering.

Scope: smin, umin, smax, umax, uadd_sat, sadd_sat, usub_sat, ssub_sat, avg_round, umulhi, smulhi, and applicable rounded/saturating multiply instructions.

Acceptance: Supported opcode/type combinations lower correctly and have focused tests; unsupported combinations fail with specific diagnostics.

title: Complete i128 arithmetic and conversion coverage
description:
Why: Current i128 support uses i64 pairs and covers only selected operations.

Scope: Remaining meaningful integer operations including div/rem, high multiply, abs, min/max, overflow/saturation, and float conversions where semantics permit.

Acceptance: Every intended i128 opcode is lowered or explicitly documented unsupported; tests cover carries, signedness, overflow, division corners, and conversions.

title: Choose SIMD representation and legalization strategy
description:
Why: Choose a representation and legalization strategy for CLIF vectors, which have no direct scalar representation in the current bridge.

Acceptance: Document vector value representation, lane order, supported widths/types, legalizations, and unsupported boundaries.
design:
Representation: extend the CLIF value map with a vector bundle: an ordered low-to-high list of Waffle V128 values. Keep scalar values as one Waffle value and i128 as its existing pair. Each bundle element represents 128 consecutive bits, with lane 0 in the least-significant bits of the first chunk, matching Wasm SIMD lane numbering and little-endian memory layout.

Fixed widths: map 64-bit CLIF vectors to one V128 with the unused upper 64 bits canonicalized to zero; map 128-bit vectors directly to one V128; map 256- and 512-bit vectors to two or four V128 chunks. Legalize lane-wise operators per chunk and explicitly normalize padding bits for sub-128-bit vectors. Cross-chunk shuffle, reductions, and other operations need operation-specific lowering.

Initial direct lane shapes: i8, i16, i32, i64, f32, and f64, matching Wasm SIMD. Other CLIF lane types may use V128 as raw bits, but arithmetic/conversions without equivalent Wasm operators remain unsupported until a separate legalization is implemented. Dynamic/scalable CLIF vectors are rejected because Wasm v128 has a fixed width and cannot represent a runtime-scaled number of lanes without a different loop/runtime ABI.

Validation: keep CLIF error fixtures for unsupported cases; when a fixture translates, the harness instructs the contributor to promote it into tests/fixtures and add interpreter-versus-Wasm run expectations. Wasmi's SIMD feature is enabled for all test builds.
notes: Investigation: portal-pc-waffle 0.5.5 exposes Type::V128 and SIMD Operator variants; its backend emits wasm_encoder SIMD instructions, and its package includes tests/roundtrip/test-simd.wat. The blocker is representation/legalization, not missing Wasm SIMD or Waffle support. Current CLIF-to-Waffle map_type rejects vectors. The new error fixture tests this boundary and the differential harness tells the contributor to move a fixture into tests/fixtures when translation succeeds. Wasmi SIMD support is enabled in the shared dev dependency for promoted runtime fixtures. Design boundary still to decide: map 128-bit fixed CLIF vectors directly to V128 first; choose split/padded legalizations or explicit rejection for narrower/wider fixed vectors and dynamic vectors.

title: Lower SIMD constants, splat, lanes, and shuffles
description:
Why: Cranelift vectors have no direct scalar representation in the current bridge.

Scope: vconst, scalar_to_vector, extract_vector, splat, shuffle, swizzle, x86_pshufb, insertlane, extractlane, vector load forms, and lane widening/narrowing operations where the chosen representation permits them.

Acceptance: Documented supported vector combinations lower correctly; tests cover lane order and boundaries; unsupported cases are explicit.

title: Complete CLIF 0.136 to Waffle instruction coverage
description:
Why: clif2wasm currently lowers a scalar subset of Cranelift 0.136 CLIF and errors on other valid instructions or type combinations. This epic tracks the remaining instruction and representation work required for broad CLIF-to-Waffle translation. Scope includes scalar, i128, SIMD, memory, control flow, and machine-specific CLIF operations; Wasm-inexpressible semantics need explicit legalization or a documented boundary.

Acceptance: Every Cranelift 0.136 opcode is either lowered correctly for supported types and semantics, or intentionally rejected with a documented reason and coverage test. Tests cover each newly supported family.

title: Spike portal-pc-waffle dependency swap for atomics
description: Determine whether portal-pc-waffle can replace waffle with manageable API changes and support shared-memory atomic emission. Build the project and validate representative atomic instructions plus shared memory configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Project compiles against portal-pc-waffle; representative atomic operators can be represented and encoded; shared memory with maximum validates; summarize migration cost and recommend whether to keep or revert the swap.
notes: The spike smoke test was temporary and was removed during the completed dependency transition, per user direction. The portal-pc-waffle dependency and API adapters remain in place.
close_reason: The portal-pc-waffle 0.5.5 swap compiles after adapting changed signature, memory, table, and reference type APIs. Added a smoke test proving shared memory with a maximum plus atomic RMW/CAS are emitted and validate. Full cargo test and diff check pass.

title: Support multi-function differential fixtures and call coverage
description: The fixture runner currently requires exactly one CLIF function, which prevents end-to-end tests of direct calls, indirect calls, and shared function-index resolution. Extend fixture loading and interpreter setup to register all parsed functions and translate them as one module.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with multiple functions can invoke a selected exported entry point. Add direct-call and call_indirect cases whose results match both the fixture expectation and the Cranelift interpreter. Include clear diagnostics for unresolved fixture function references.
close_reason: Fixture runner now supports multiple CLIF functions and selectable entries; direct and indirect calls match interpreter/wasm results, and unresolved fixture callees have a diagnostic regression fixture.

title: Add differential coverage for CLIF memory operations and stack slots
description: Current fixtures exercise scalar returns but do not cover the translator's load/store and shadow-stack paths. Add CLIF fixtures using stack_addr and stack slots so memory behavior can be checked by both the Cranelift interpreter and wasm runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Cover load/store offsets, narrow signed and unsigned loads, truncating stores, and stack-slot frame setup. Each fixture compares the interpreter and wasm results and checks explicit expected values; emitted wasm validates before execution.
close_reason: Added differential fixtures for stack frame setup, offset load/store, signed and unsigned narrow loads, and truncating stores; Wasmi validates and executes each module against Cranelift interpreter results.

title: Compare expected traps in differential CLIF fixtures
description: The fixture runner currently treats a trap in either runtime as a harness failure, so it cannot test CLIF traps or wasm trap equivalence. Add a fixture directive for expected traps and compare interpreter and wasm outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures can declare a call expected to trap. The runner passes when both Cranelift interpretation and wasm execution trap, and reports a useful failure when only one traps or either returns. Cover explicit trap and integer division by zero.
close_reason: Added ; trap: fixture directives and differential outcome checks; explicit void/value traps and signed division by zero trap in both engines.

title: Handle unreachable CLIF blocks during function translation
description:
## Context
The bridge creates a waffle block for every laid-out CLIF block but only translates blocks in reachable CFG reverse postorder. Unreachable blocks can therefore be left without terminators, causing later validation or emission failures. Give unreachable blocks an explicit translation policy.

## Steps to Reproduce
Translate a function with an entry block that returns and a second laid-out block with a valid terminator that has no incoming edge. The block is allocated in waffle but omitted from reachable CFG translation.

## Acceptance Criteria
A valid function containing an unreachable laid-out block either translates to valid wasm with the unreachable block terminated, or fails during preflight with a clear unsupported-input error. Add a differential fixture and validate the emitted module.
acceptance_criteria: A valid function containing an unreachable laid-out block either translates to valid wasm with the unreachable block terminated, or fails during preflight with a clear unsupported-input error. Add a differential fixture and validate the emitted module.
close_reason: Unreachable laid-out blocks without translated terminators now receive an explicit unreachable terminator; differential fixture validates and executes the emitted wasm.
